system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the fourth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
These 3 questions belong together and follow one another in the test booklet.

## Question 1

A. Draw 1 straight line on this rectangle to divide it into 2 triangles.

[Image: Rectangle]

Figure, described in words:
An outline of an empty rectangle, wider than it is tall, with horizontal top and bottom sides and vertical left and right sides.

## Question 2

B. Draw 1 straight line on this rectangle to divide it into 2 rectangles.

[Image: Rectangle]

Figure, described in words:
An outline of an empty rectangle, wider than it is tall, with horizontal top and bottom sides and vertical left and right sides.

## Question 3

C. Draw 2 straight lines on this rectangle to divide it into 1 rectangle and 2 triangles.

[Image: Rectangle]

Figure, described in words:
An outline of an empty rectangle, wider than it is tall, with horizontal top and bottom sides and vertical left and right sides.

Answer each of the 3 questions.

answer_1.description: Your answer to question 1, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_1.title: Answer 1

answer_2.description: Your answer to question 2, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_2.title: Answer 2

answer_3.description: Your answer to question 3, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_3.title: Answer 3

output.answer_1: Draw one straight diagonal line from one corner of the rectangle to the opposite corner (for example, from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner). This divides the rectangle into 2 triangles, each with a right angle at one corner of the rectangle.
output.answer_2: Draw one straight line that goes across the rectangle from one side to the opposite side, parallel to the left and right sides (a vertical line) or parallel to the top and bottom sides (a horizontal line), placed so that it splits the rectangle into 2 smaller rectangles. For example, draw a vertical line down the middle of the rectangle.
output.answer_3: Draw one straight line from a corner of the rectangle diagonally across to a point on the opposite side, and draw a second straight line parallel to the top side (or bottom side) that cuts across the rectangle, so that the figure is divided into 1 rectangle and 2 triangles: one triangle formed by the diagonal line at one end, the rectangle in the middle, and a second triangle at the other end. For example, draw a diagonal from the top-left corner down to the bottom side at the middle, then draw a horizontal line from the left side to the diagonal line at the same height as the bottom-right region's apex.
